child: When did you last do something just because it made you happy? Do it today!
adult: When was the last time you did something simply because it made you happy? Make time for it today.

child: Spend 20 minutes on {activity} – just for you.
adult: Give yourself 30 unhurried minutes of {activity}, just for you.

child: Draw a picture of how you feel today. Is it sunny, rainy or stormy inside?
adult: Write down three words for how you are really feeling today – not how you think you should feel.

child: Find a quiet spot and take 5 slow balloon-breaths. What do you notice?
adult: Take a 10-minute walk alone without your phone. Notice what your mind keeps returning to.

child: Write or draw 3 things you are good at.
adult: Write down three things you have handled well lately, however small.

child: What is something you used to love doing when you were little? Try it again.
adult: Think of something you loved before life got busy. Do a small version of it this week.

child: Make a 'happy box' – put in 3 things that make you smile.
adult: Make a list of 5 small things that refill you. Stick it somewhere you'll see it.

child: Tell someone one thing you need today (a hug, quiet time, help with something).
adult: Notice one need you have been ignoring. Name it to someone you trust.

child: Make a 'me map': draw yourself in the middle and all the things you love around you.
adult: Write a short letter to yourself from five years ago. What would they want you to remember?

child: Choose a song that feels like YOU. Play it and dance or listen with eyes closed.
adult: Go somewhere new on your own for an hour – a café, a trail, a gallery. Notice how it feels.

child: Lie on the grass or your bed and look at the clouds or ceiling for 5 minutes. What shapes or thoughts come?
adult: Sit somewhere quiet for 5 minutes with no phone and nothing to do. Notice what you feel when you stop.

child: Pick your favourite snack and eat it really slowly. What does it taste like?
adult: Make yourself a drink you love and have it slowly, sitting down, without doing anything else.

child: Finish this sentence: 'I feel most like me when…' Draw or write it.
adult: Finish this sentence: 'I feel most like myself when…' Then plan one way to do more of it.

child: Make a playlist of 5 songs that match your moods: happy, sad, angry, calm, excited.
adult: Make a playlist of songs that fit different parts of your life. Which one surprised you?

child: Try something new by yourself today – a new game, a new drawing style, a new food.
adult: Try one small new thing today, just to see how it feels – a new route, recipe or hobby.

child: Write down one worry, fold it up and put it in a 'worry jar'. You don't have to carry it all day.
adult: Write down what is on your mind, then choose one thing you can let go of for today.

child: Give yourself a 'superpower name' for something you're good at. Draw your superhero self!
adult: Write down a strength people have noticed in you, even if you're not sure you believe it yet.

child: Spend 15 minutes on {activity} without anyone helping or watching – just you.
adult: Do {activity} alone this week – not to get better at it, just to enjoy it.

child: Think of a time you were brave. Tell someone about it or draw it.
adult: Think of a hard time you got through. What helped you? Write it down so you remember.

child: Make a 'calm corner' with a blanket, a soft toy and something nice to look at.
adult: Create a small calm space at home – a chair, a candle, a blanket – and use it once this week.

child: Say 3 kind things to yourself in the mirror. They can be silly!
adult: Notice how you talk to yourself today. Try saying one thing to yourself you would say to a friend.

child: What makes you laugh the most? Find it and do it today.
adult: When did you last really laugh? Find something that made you laugh before and go back to it.
